definitions.explanation: Protective body covering worn by warriors, especially the traditional Japanese armor worn by samurai. Also used figuratively for emotional defenses or outward facades.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}に{鎧|よろい}が{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: Armor is on display at the museum.

examples.japanese: {武士|ぶし}は{鎧|よろい}を{身|み}につけて{戦|たたか}った。
{端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}には{鎧|よろい}や{兜|かぶと}を{飾|かざ}る{家庭|かてい}もある。
examples.english: Some families display armor and helmets for the Boys' Day festival.

notes:
Refers specifically to Japanese-style armor unless otherwise qualified. Western-style armor is usually distinguished as {西洋|せいよう}の{鎧|よろい}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鎧|よろい}を{着|き}る / {鎧|よろい}を{身|み}につける (to put on armor)
- {鎧|よろい}{兜|かぶと} (armor and helmet — a set phrase)
- {鎧|よろい}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ (to remove armor; figuratively, to drop one's guard)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese armor ({鎧|よろい}) is displayed during {端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく} (Boys' Day, May 5) as a symbol of strength and protection for boys.
